source.title: Latent Adversarial Training Improves the Representation of Refusal
source.authors: Alexander R. Abbas; N. Petrova; H. Lyons; Natalia Perez-Campanero

record.file_problem: No material truncation or wrong-document issue; the text includes the paper, references, and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study computes harmful-minus-harmless activation differences and applies directional ablation across layers and token positions, directly reproducing the original measurement and intervention in Llama-2-7B-chat training variants.
record.gate_note: The paper reports post-ablation refusal rates, SVD variance explained, qualitative PCA separability, and a qualitative layer-wise ablation result. The cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows. Fine-grained values visible only in figures are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Uses Arditi et al.'s method: a difference-in-means direction at layer 14 from 100 AdvBench/Alpaca pairs, ablated at every layer and token. It reports post-ablation refusal rates on 520 harmful prompts for three Llama-2-7B-chat training variants (SSFT, embedding AT, LAT). It also applies directions across variants and runs a non-causal SVD/PCA of harmful-minus-harmless activation differences.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with three corrections. First, the authors also claim LAT shows improved robustness to vectors from other models. The table only partly supports this: baseline→LAT gives 25.77%, above baseline self 20.38%, but no other-source vector was tested on LAT. Second, the Discussion calls the robustness gain marginal and not definitive. Third, the authors say LAT's encoding is more concentrated and better approximated by a single vector. That conflicts with their PCA reading of a more complex, non-single-direction encoding and with the 20% second SVD component.
record.recipe_differences: The study follows the original difference-in-means and directional-ablation approach, deriving the direction at the last token in layer 14 from 100 harmful-harmless pairs and ablating across layers and token positions. It tests SSFT, embedding-space AT, and LAT variants of one model; it does not test direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Training variant changes the reported post-ablation refusal rates and SVD distribution. The PCA analysis covers layers 1, 2, 8, and 20; the layer-wise analysis reports layer 14 as most effective.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial fine-tuning changes robustness to refusal-direction ablation. Embedding-space AT raises self-ablation residual refusal to 38.08% from 20.38% (SSFT). Untargeted latent AT lowers it to 16.92%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic adversarial training (not targeted at the refusal direction) alters robustness to refusal-direction ablation; embedding AT helps, untargeted LAT does not.

record.code_released: https://github.com/thestephencasper/latent_adversarial_training (published training framework used; release of this study's own code not stated)
record.problems: Only Llama-2-7B-chat training variants are evaluated. The refusal-rate table reports post-ablation values but no unablated reference rates. No direction-addition test or general-capability evaluation is reported. The authors note limits to generalization across architectures, scales, models, and datasets. Some layer-wise and PCA results are qualitative in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported numeric table results were left out. Fine-grained layer-wise values in Appendix C, Figure 4 and visual PCA details in Appendix B, Figure 3 are not transcribed because the supplied text provides no recoverable numeric values.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; preservation of general capabilities; unablated refusal baseline not reported.
All: no weight edit or abliteration of released models.
All: jailbreaks are not analysed, and no training targets direction ablation (LAT is untargeted L2 noise at layer 4).
Causal comparison of affine, cone or multi-direction ablation; the evidence is SVD/PCA only.
Transfer across languages, from base to instruct models, and across model families or sizes.
When refusal is trained (timing or stage); only the fine-tuning method varies.

missing.what: LAT model shows unusually high invalid-response rates under layer-specific ablation at early layers 2–4; the record has no row for this possible capability or coherence cost.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper with one model family and size. The refusal direction is computed at layer 14 and ablated at all layers. No unablated refusal rate is given, so all partial or observed states assume near-total baseline refusal of AdvBench by Llama-2-7B-chat; the paper does not state this. V3 links were removed from r1–r7: LAT is untargeted latent perturbation, not training against direction ablation, and ablation is not a jailbreak. The LAT finding is placed under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Addition of the direction and preservation of general capabilities were not tested; no pre-ablation refusal rate is reported.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration procedure was tested.
Training against the direction's ablation was not tested.
The study measures SVD/PCA structure but does not causally compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction interventions.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Transfer is tested among SSFT, embedding-space AT, and LAT variants of Llama 2 7B only; transfer across languages, base-to-instruct models, or other model families is not tested.
The study compares SSFT, embedding-space AT, and LAT, but does not vary when refusal training occurs.

source_check.notes: The header says code: y, but the text releases no code of its own; it only cites Casper's LAT training code. The text does not say how refusals were judged, does not give the SVD layer, token or pair count, and gives no unablated refusal rates. The LAT vs SSFT self-ablation 95% CIs overlap. Section 4.3 (figure only) says layer 14 is the most effective ablation layer in all variants, i.e. LAT does not move refusal across layers. That bears on V7 and is not in the checked rows.

statements.correction: Baseline = released Llama-2-7b-chat (Meta SSFT); authors trained the AT and LAT adapters with Casper et al.'s code.
